decision: OBJECT -- 0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX. The subject is unmoved at the dispatched digest 473072ec... and mode 0444, and the frozen turn-1 subject is unmoved and unedited at 65d46fcb.... The turn-1 SHOULD-FIX landed in full and landed correctly: all four frozen siblings are pinned in the Measured-inputs table with digests that recompute exactly, and all four are named operatively in the remeasurement clause, producing a custody set that is a strict superset of D-238 turn 2's. Sixteen of sixteen cited digests reproduce with zero unmatched, both Stage A verdicts are ACCEPT 0/0 at mode 0444, the Stage A observation-honesty clause is exact including its refusal to invent a Codex identifier, every live register figure re-measures correctly from file 08 at HEAD, and a programmatic scan of D-170 through D-239 confirms D-236 is the sole cell-edit entry, so the stated no-cell-edit range omits exactly one member and omits the right one. A full diff against the frozen turn-1 subject shows no scope creep: every prohibition, both Decision items, Readiness effect and Reversibility are byte-identical. All eighteen dispatch attacks fail. One independent attack lands. The turn-1 disposition block records only CLAUDE-D240-SF1 and drops both identified turn-1 observations, CLAUDE-D240-O1 and CLAUDE-D240-O2, which appear nowhere in the subject. Across the whole repository, identified turn-1 COORD observation identifiers exist in exactly three cycles -- D-211, which CONSENTed at turn 1 and owed no disposition; D-238, whose turn-2 draft carried its identifier as an OBSERVATION row and whose adopted entry names both Stage A and Stage B Claude identifiers with the no-invented-Codex-identifier limb; and D-240, which is the first to drop them. The draft performs this exact discipline for Stage A one screen later, so the safe form is already in the subject and is simply withheld from Stage B; and one of the dropped observations, CLAUDE-D240-O1, was in fact acted on, since the SF1 rows restored the per-version anchors it recorded. Nothing asserted is false -- '0 MUST-FIX, 1 SHOULD-FIX' is literally exact, because observations are not findings -- so this is incompleteness of the record against a same-lineage convention, scored SHOULD-FIX, the same class as the turn-1 finding the drafter accepted. The remedy is two table rows, confined to the D-240 draft, touching nothing frozen and no register cell.
